content:
Good puzzle and good progression in the tests, well done! A few corrections needed before I can approve personally:

- What rounding algorithm? If multiple work, please provide them, to ensure cross-language compatibility.
- Some tests and validators are unnamed.

Formatting
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly as described in the points below.

Goal
* Please format N as a [[variable]].

* Please format 0, 100 and 0.4 as {{constants}}.

* Please format all keywords in <<bold>>.

Input
* Please format N and X as [[variables]].

* Please format "Line 1" and "Next [[N]] lines" in <<bold>>.

Output
* Please format "Line 1" and "Line 2" in <<bold>>.

* Line 1: Please remove the example.

* Line 1: Please specify whether to *round* or *truncate* Target Value to 2 decimal places.

Constraints
* Please format N and X as [[variables]].

Input/Cases
* If the chosen numbers are always in ascending order, please specify that in the input description. Otherwise, please randomise the order of the chosen numbers in some of the cases.

Cases
* Please remove all trailing newlines from:
  • the input for all cases except Test 1.
  • the output for all cases.

* Each test and its validator should cover the *same scenario* with slightly different inputs and slightly different outputs (if applicable). Please split the current 4 pairs of cases into 8 accordingly.

Thanks.
Hey, thanks for the feedback! Well,I've updated it! Lemme know if there're any corrections that need to be done to get it approved!

No problem 🙂

The cases still need a bit more work:

* Validator 8: Please remove the trailing newline from the output.

* It's good that each case pair now covers the same scenario. However, the expected outputs should also differ slightly whenever possible, rather than every test expecting exactly the same output as its corresponding validator.

* In most of the visible tests, the chosen numbers are in ascending order. Please revise at least half of them so that the numbers appear in a random order.

* In the previous version there are cases with large player pool (i.e. N ≥ 10). Please:

  • add a case pair with N between 21 and 30.

  • add a case pair with N between 41 and 50.

* Please also make sure the chosen numbers are generated randomly in the new cases.

Thanks.

Done! Different test cases define the actual difficulty level rising with each test case.

Thanks!

Cases
* The cases listed below look good, but please consider renaming them, as their current names don't reflect what the cases are testing (e.g. not tie breakers, not sorted):
  • Absolute Tie-Breaker (Equidistant Matches) (Test 4)
  • Dual Value Tie-Breaker (Test 5)
  • High Number Clustering (Sorted) (Test 6)
  • Low Decimals Precision Rounding (Sorted) (Test 7)
  • Floating Point Halfway Tie (Sorted) (Test 8)

* Could you also add two pairs of genuine tie-breaker cases: one pair with N < 10 and another with N > 25?

Thanks.
Done! Now, is it ready to be approved?

The new cases still need some changes.

Cases
* Small Pool Tie-Breaker (Test 11): Please swap 6 and 14.

Validator 11: There's no tie-breaker.

Large Pool Tie-Breaker (Validator 11): Please swap 24 with one of the 52s in the middle.

Validator 12: Please swap 34 with one of the 78s in the middle.

Thanks.
Done! You were right there was no tie - breaker, but now its fixed.

Thanks for the quick fix. Please swap 12 and 18 in Validator 11.

All the swaps mentioned are to make sure to verify that the player's solution should switch to the correct answer when it finds a smaller answer with the same difference as the larger number found earlier in each list.
